limitations: This is descriptive attribution of an already frozen cashbook, not a new configuration or counterfactual portfolio replay.
The ZEN/USELESS priority decision is established, but choosing the later winner is hindsight. No alternative ranking profitability is established.
ZEN had higher relative volume while USELESS had larger TR expansion; there is no prevalidated scalar strength ranking in this experiment.
1H and4H statistics summarize different candidate populations; they do not isolate a causal effect of timeframe or entry delay.
Cross-venue copies must not be added as independent economic wins. ZEC duplicate rejection did not mean the asset was missed.
Foregone event returns cannot be added to account return: exposure, intervening cashbooks, liquidity, exits and replacement signals would change.
Cash and slot statistics use documented clocks; cash at the close can reflect exits occurring after the opening slot count.
The study is retrospective and previously viewed. Funding/real impact are not fully covered.
